provider: git-annex git-lfs special remote (annex over any LFS host)

free_tier.stated: N/A. A protocol adapter. Turns ANY git-lfs server (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, a self-hosted Gitea) into an annex special remote, so the LFS host's quota applies but annex adds hash-verified partial clone and `whereis` across mirrors.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: | Cannot delete = every mistake is permanent on the LFS side, and the host's month-storage accounting (GitHub) means you keep paying for it in quota

egress.terms: Determined by the underlying Git LFS host.

tooling: `git annex initremote lfstest type=git-lfs url=... encryption=shared`. Supports gcrypt:: URL prefix for encrypting the git side too.
chaining: Because annex can hold the same content on several LFS remotes, you can stack the 10 GiB/project GitLab allowance and the 10 GiB GitHub allowance as tiers of one logical dataset, with annex tracking which objects live where. Sharding a 1 TiB corpus across 100 GitLab projects becomes a `git annex copy --to` loop.
limits_note: Hard, documented limitations: 'The git-lfs protocol does not support deleting content, so git-annex cannot delete anything from a git-lfs special remote'; no upload resume; 'git-annex doesn't do batching. This may cause it to fall afoul of rate limiting of git-lfs servers' — which directly collides with GitLab's 1000 req/min LFS limit. Requires SHA256 backend for efficiency.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Cannot delete = every mistake is permanent on the LFS side, and the host's month-storage accounting (GitHub) means you keep paying for it in quota. No batching + per-object request = the exact workload LFS rate limits are designed to stop.

evidence.proved: example: 'git annex initremote lfstest type=git-lfs url=gcrypt::git@github.com:username/somerepo.git encryption=shared'
